docs.text:
Suomenkielinen ohje: Kilowahti suomeksi

Kilowahti (kilowatti + vahti — "the kilowatt sentinel") is a Home Assistant integration for European electricity cost awareness and optimization — whether you are on a spot contract or a fixed rate.

It fetches day-ahead hourly or 15-minute spot prices, primarily from Kilowahti's own content delivery network (CDN), which fetches the data directly from ENTSO-E, and automatically falls back to spot-hinta.fi. It applies your VAT and, if you want, transfer pricing (e.g. separate day and night or seasonal tariffs), and exposes sensors, binary sensors, and services you can use in automations, dashboards, and energy management scripts.

docs.title: Main features
docs.text:
Prices

  • Day-ahead spot prices — no API key or other integration required, 15-minute or 1-hour resolution
  • Transfer price groups and tiers with schedules and monthly fees
  • Fixed-price contract period management — when a fixed period is active, the fixed price is automatically shown as the active price instead of the spot price
  • Monthly electricity contract base fee spread as a daily cost sensor

Control

  • Price rank, rank quartile, and total price rank sensors
  • Control factor sensors (0–1 and bipolar ±1) for proportional automation
  • Writable price and rank threshold number entities — adjust limits from the dashboard or automations without reopening configuration
  • Optimization scores measuring how well consumption is shifted to cheap hours
  • Rolling average sensors for the next 30/60/120 minutes (only with 15-minute prices)

Generation & export (optional, enabled in Advanced options)

  • Export price sensors and daily statistics
  • Import/export spread and self-consumption value sensors
  • Best export window and best charge window services
  • Solar generation schedule service

Battery optimization (optional, requires battery capacity configured)

  • Charge opportunity factor and categorical charge recommendation sensors
  • Optimal charge window start/end sensors
  • charge_from_grid_recommended and discharge_to_grid_recommended binary sensors

Home Assistant services

  • Query prices and export prices for any time range
  • Find cheapest consecutive windows for scheduling appliances
  • Manage fixed-price periods via service calls

docs.title: Supported regions
docs.text: Kilowahti shows electricity prices in Finland and 29 other European countries — see the full list of supported regions.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Install from the Marketplace (Home Assistant 2026.11 and newer) or HACS (older versions)
  2. Start the setup wizard — the Marketplace opens it after installing; with HACS go to Settings → Devices & Services → Add Integration → Kilowahti
  3. Complete the setup wizard
  4. Use the sensors in your dashboards and automations

First setup walks through everything you need to get started in about ten minutes, including which wizard answers you can skip at first and how you build a first automation.

That cut-and-paste solution was the direct role model for this integration; it proved the idea works, gave direction to the sensor design, and created automation templates that many Finnish HA users have relied on. A special thanks also to the Finnish hobbyist behind spot-hinta.fi for building and maintaining an excellent, free, and easy-to-use electricity price API that makes projects like this possible. docs.title: Automation examples
docs.text:
2026-03-092026-11-05

These examples use {name} as a placeholder for the name you set during configuration. If the name you set is Home, replace {name} with home in entity IDs.

Starting out?

Kilowahti provides its own triggers and conditions that you can pick straight from the automation editor — no entity IDs, no YAML. The examples below build the same behaviour from entities, which is what you need once you go beyond what those cover.

docs.title: Run during cheap hours (rank-based)
docs.text:
The simplest approach: use the rank_acceptable binary sensor to gate an automation. Set your acceptable rank threshold in the Kilowahti options.

Rank follows the energy price you actually pay. On a spot contract that is the market ordering; during a fixed-price period every hour costs the same, so every slot ranks 1 and rank_acceptable stays on all day. That is deliberate — there is no cheaper hour to wait for — but if you want a gate that still narrows the day on a fixed contract, work from total_price_rank, which includes transfer — either with a numeric state condition on the sensor, or with the built-in "price is lowest today" condition and "became cheapest slot" trigger, both of which rank by total price.

alias: Heat water during cheap hours
triggers:
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: binary_sensor.kilowahti_{name}_rank_acceptable
    to: "on"
actions:
  - action: switch.turn_on
    target:
      entity_id: switch.water_heater

To stop the device when the window ends:

alias: Stop water heater when hours no longer cheap
triggers:
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: binary_sensor.kilowahti_{name}_rank_acceptable
    to: "off"
actions:
  - action: switch.turn_off
    target:
      entity_id: switch.water_heater

docs.title: Run when price is below threshold
docs.text:
Use price_acceptable when you care about the absolute price rather than relative rank. Set your threshold in Kilowahti options.

alias: EV charging when price is acceptable
triggers:
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: binary_sensor.kilowahti_{name}_price_acceptable
    to: "on"
actions:
  - action: switch.turn_on
    target:
      entity_id: switch.ev_charger

You can also combine both conditions using price_or_rank_acceptable:

triggers:
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: binary_sensor.kilowahti_{name}_price_or_rank_acceptable
    to: "on"

docs.title: Schedule appliance at cheapest upcoming window
docs.text:
Use the kilowahti.cheapest_hours service to find the cheapest consecutive block ahead of time and schedule your appliance to start then. Requires an input_datetime helper — create one via Settings → Devices & Services → Helpers → Create helper → Date and/or time (e.g. input_datetime.cheapest_window_start).

Automation 1 — Find the window (runs daily at 17:00):

alias: Find cheapest 3-hour overnight window
triggers:
  - trigger: time
    at: "17:00:00"
actions:
  - action: kilowahti.cheapest_hours
    data:
      start: "{{ now().isoformat() }}"
      end: "{{ (now() + timedelta(hours=15)).isoformat() }}"  # 15 hours is the window from 17:00 → 08:00 next morning
      hours: 3
    response_variable: result
  - action: input_datetime.set_datetime
    data:
      datetime: "{{ result['start'] | as_datetime | as_local }}"
    target:
      entity_id: input_datetime.cheapest_window_start

Automation 2 — Start the appliance at the scheduled time:

alias: Start dishwasher at cheapest window
triggers:
  - trigger: time
    at: input_datetime.cheapest_window_start
actions:
  - action: switch.turn_on
    target:
      entity_id: switch.dishwasher

docs.title: Proportional control (thermostat / climate)
docs.text:
Use control_factor_price to modulate a setpoint rather than switching on/off. 1.0 = cheapest slot, 0.0 = most expensive.

This example adjusts a thermostat setpoint between 19 °C (expensive) and 22 °C (cheap) using 0.5 °C steps:

alias: Adjust thermostat by price
triggers:
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: sensor.kilowahti_{name}_control_factor_price
actions:
  - action: climate.set_temperature
    data:
      temperature: >
        {{ (19 + (states('sensor.kilowahti_{name}_control_factor_price') | float(0)) * 3) | round(0, "half") }}
    target:
      entity_id: climate.living_room

For a ±1 bipolar input (e.g. to feed a PID controller), use sensor.kilowahti_{name}_control_factor_price_bipolar instead.

Note

The control factor shape (linear or sinusoidal) and scaling exponent are configurable in Kilowahti options. Sinusoidal gives a gentler response near the extremes.

Tip

Home Assistant ships an improved version of Jinja's round filter — including the "half" method used above, which rounds to the nearest 0.5. See Home Assistant's round documentation.

docs.title: Scale EV charging current by price
docs.text:
Rather than switching an EV charger on or off, use control_factor_price to continuously scale the charging current between a minimum and maximum. 1.0 = cheapest slot (full current), 0.0 = most expensive slot (minimum current).

This example scales between 6 A and 16 A using 1 A steps:

alias: Scale EV charging current by price
triggers:
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: sensor.kilowahti_{name}_control_factor_price
actions:
  - action: number.set_value
    target:
      entity_id: number.ev_charger_current
    data:
      value: >
        {{ (6 + (states('sensor.kilowahti_{name}_control_factor_price') | float(0)) * 10) | round(0) | int }}

Adjust 6 (minimum current) and 10 (spread: maximum minus minimum) to your charger's supported range. Check your charger's integration documentation for the correct entity and accepted values.

docs.title: Charge and discharge a battery by quartile
docs.text:
Use price_quartile to drive a home battery: charge in the cheapest 25% of slots (Q1), discharge in the most expensive 25% (Q4), and leave it on automatic otherwise.

alias: Battery charge/discharge by price quartile
triggers:
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: sensor.kilowahti_{name}_price_quartile
actions:
  - choose:
      - conditions:
          - condition: state
            entity_id: sensor.kilowahti_{name}_price_quartile
            state: "1"
        sequence:
          - action: select.select_option
            target:
              entity_id: select.battery_mode
            data:
              option: charge
      - conditions:
          - condition: state
            entity_id: sensor.kilowahti_{name}_price_quartile
            state: "4"
        sequence:
          - action: select.select_option
            target:
              entity_id: select.battery_mode
            data:
              option: discharge
    default:
      - action: select.select_option
        target:
          entity_id: select.battery_mode
        data:
          option: auto

Replace select.battery_mode and the option values with the entities and modes your battery integration exposes.

docs.title: Notify when tomorrow's prices are available
docs.text:
Tomorrow's prices are published in the early afternoon (around 13:00 CET; later in some markets). Trigger on the tomorrow's-prices-available binary sensor turning on to send a push notification with the day's price range.

alias: Notify when tomorrow's prices arrive
triggers:
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: binary_sensor.kilowahti_{name}_tomorrow_available
    to: "on"
actions:
  - action: notify.mobile_app_your_phone
    data:
      title: "Tomorrow's electricity prices"
      message: >
        Min {{ states('sensor.kilowahti_{name}_tomorrow_spot_minimum') }},
        avg {{ states('sensor.kilowahti_{name}_tomorrow_spot_average') }},
        max {{ states('sensor.kilowahti_{name}_tomorrow_spot_maximum') }}
        {{ state_attr('sensor.kilowahti_{name}_tomorrow_spot_minimum', 'unit_of_measurement') }}

Replace notify.mobile_app_your_phone with your notification service.

docs.title: Alert when spot price exceeds today's average
docs.text:
Send a notification whenever the current slot price rises above today's average — useful as an early warning to delay discretionary loads.

alias: Alert when price exceeds today's average
triggers:
  - trigger: template
    value_template: >
      {{ states('sensor.kilowahti_{name}_spot_price') | float(0) >
         states('sensor.kilowahti_{name}_today_spot_average') | float(0) }}
actions:
  - action: notify.mobile_app_your_phone
    data:
      message: >
        Electricity price {{ states('sensor.kilowahti_{name}_spot_price') }}
        is above today's average {{ states('sensor.kilowahti_{name}_today_spot_average') }}
        {{ state_attr('sensor.kilowahti_{name}_spot_price', 'unit_of_measurement') }}.

docs.title: Version 2026.11.0 (2026-11-04)
docs.text:
This release makes Kilowahti's entity IDs independent of the Home Assistant language, with a one-click repair that migrates existing installs. It also adds a rename flow for entries, a repair issue for stuck fallback sources and icons for the distinctive entities, makes Kilowahti ready for the Home Assistant Marketplace, and continues the quality-scale work started in 2026.9.0.

New

  • Entity IDs no longer depend on the Home Assistant language: new installs get sensor.kilowahti_home_spot_price in every language instead of localized variants such as sensor.kilowahti_home_spot_hinta; displayed names stay translated
  • Repair that offers existing installs a one-click rename of display-name entity IDs to the stable ones; nothing is renamed until you confirm, entities whose ID you changed yourself are never touched, and history and statistics are kept
  • The repair's confirmation lists the automations, scripts, scenes and groups that use the entities (dashboards, templates and external systems are not checked); references to the old IDs must be updated by hand afterwards
  • Reconfigure flow to rename an entry; the entry's title and unique ID follow the new name, other settings stay untouched and the name cannot clash with another entry
  • Repair issue when a region has been served by a fallback price source for over 24 hours; it clears automatically once the primary source is back
  • Icons for the price data source, active transfer tier, active fixed period, fixed-period active, tomorrow available and threshold entities
  • Integration category (Energy › Energy prices) for the Home Assistant Marketplace and HACS catalog

Changed

  • Entity keys renamed for consistency (for example today_avg → today_average); existing entities are migrated in place and keep their entity IDs, history and settings. Downgrading to an earlier release afterwards re-creates the renamed entities as duplicates, so remove the leftovers from the entity registry if you roll back
  • Services are registered when the integration loads instead of when the first entry is set up, and stay available after the last entry is unloaded
  • Service errors (no entries, unknown entry or period id, invalid or overlapping fixed period) are now translatable validation errors; automations that catch the old error type need to catch ServiceValidationError
  • Multi-entry service, trigger and condition lookups skip entries that failed setup
  • Installation instructions cover the Home Assistant Marketplace (2026.11 and newer) alongside HACS
  • New strings translated into all 24 languages (machine-assisted; corrections welcome)

docs.title: Version 2026.9.0 (2026-09-27)
docs.text:
This release centers on Total Price Arrays — a new option to expose per-slot energy, transfer, and rank breakdowns on the total_price sensor, built from a user request. Alongside it: transfer tiers are now viewable and editable after setup, and the control factor family has been harmonized onto one consistent scale. This release also marks the first batch of work toward Home Assistant's integration quality scale, starting with diagnostics support and duplicate-entry protection.

⚠️ Breaking changes

Control factor

  • Transfer control factor polarity flipped: control_factor_transfer and control_factor_transfer_bipolar now read 1.0 for the cheapest tier (was 0.0) — update automations that depend on the raw value
  • Rank-based sensors and conditions (price_rank, price_quartile, control_factor_price*, rank trigger/condition, rank_acceptable) now respect the active fixed-price tier instead of raw spot rank — primarily affects fixed-price contract users

New

Price arrays

  • New "Expose total price arrays as sensor attributes" toggle in Advanced options: total_price publishes today_prices/tomorrow_prices attributes with energy, transfer, price, and rank per slot

Quality

  • Diagnostics support — download redacted config and coordinator state for support requests

Transfer tiers

  • Transfer tiers can now be viewed and edited after setup (price, schedule, priority), in both the initial and options flow
  • transfer_price sensor gains tariff, group, and tier attributes naming the active tariff

Control factor

  • New control_factor_total, control_factor_total_bipolar, and control_factor_transfer_bipolar sensors, joining the existing control factor family

Changed

Transfer tiers

  • Tier and fixed-period prices in the flow lists are now padded to two decimals, keeping up to five when rounding would lose the value

Price arrays

  • Tomorrow's total price array is now available during a fixed-price period even before spot prices have been fetched
  • Price array attributes (today_prices, tomorrow_prices) are excluded from the recorder database — they were large enough to make the recorder silently drop all attributes on the affected states

Quality

  • A config entry with a duplicate name now aborts setup instead of creating a confusing duplicate
  • Minimum supported Home Assistant version raised to 2026.7 (required by the trigger and condition platforms)

Other

  • Shortened the tomorrow_available binary sensor's default name — new installs get a shorter entity ID; existing entities keep theirs

Fixed

Control factor

  • Corrected the Norwegian translation of the transfer control factor name

docs.title: Version 2026.8.0 (2026-08-03)
docs.text:
New

  • Europe-wide: 43 bidding zones across 30 countries, with per-region VAT and unit presets
  • Automatic price source chain: first-party Kilowahti CDN (ENTSO-E data, all 43 zones) with spot-hinta.fi fallback in Nordic and Baltic zones only; price_data_source diagnostic sensor shows the active source

Changed

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
2026-03-092026-11-05

The setup wizard starts when you first add the integration. All settings can be edited later via Settings → Devices & Services → Kilowahti → [the name you set] → Configure (gear icon).

This page documents every field of the settings. For a first setup, First setup goes through the most essential settings and recommendations for them, and tells you which steps you can skip at the start.

docs.title: 1. Basic settings
docs.text: Field Description Name Used in entity names, e.g. Home → sensor.kilowahti_home_spot_price. Price region Your electricity market bidding zone (more information on the supported regions page) Price resolution 15 minutes (96 slots/day) or 1 hour (24 slots/day), choose the right one according to the metering interval of your electricity contract Display unit Minor or major unit of your display currency, per kWh, e.g. c/kWh or €/kWh in the eurozone, öre/kWh or kr/kWh in Sweden

docs.title: Price data
docs.text: Prices are fetched automatically, so there is nothing to configure in the settings for that. Kilowahti fetches prices primarily from its own service (the Kilowahti CDN, based on data from the EU's ENTSO-E Transparency Platform) and in case of problems uses spot-hinta.fi as a fallback. The diagnostic sensor price_data_source shows which source is currently in use.

docs.title: Display currency (non-EUR regions only)
docs.text:
European electricity markets trade in euros, so the price data available to Kilowahti is always in euros. For the bidding zones where customers are billed in a local currency, the settings have one extra step for choosing the display currency:

Field Description Display currency EUR or the region's local currency (e.g. SEK) Exchange rate source Automatic (daily ECB reference rate) or manual Manual exchange rate Amount of local currency per one EUR; this value is used in manual mode and as fallback when the automatic rate is unavailable

Spot prices are converted from EUR with a daily exchange rate that stays frozen for the whole day, so a slot's price does not change during the day even if the exchange rate fluctuates. All prices you enter (commission, transfer tiers, fixed periods, thresholds) are always in the selected display currency, and changing the currency converts the entered prices automatically using the exchange rate in the settings. After changing the display currency, check your entered prices for unintended changes caused by conversion or rounding.

Serbia (RS) and North Macedonia (MK) are not covered by the European Central Bank (ECB) reference rates, so those regions can only use a manually set exchange rate.

Long-term statistics

Changing the display currency changes the unit of every price entity. Home Assistant's long-term statistics do not convert old data in the database. Statistics recorded in the previous unit will show a unit mismatch. If you use long-term statistics and want to avoid problems, pick the currency once correctly at setup and do not change it afterwards.

docs.title: 2. VAT & electricity tax
docs.text:
The fields are pre-filled with the defaults of the selected region, and they usually do not need changing.

You can also enter your electricity contract's monthly fixed fee here, in which case it is spread across the days of the month and shown as a daily cost sensor that can be used to calculate an estimated daily cost.

Entered prices include VAT

All prices you enter elsewhere in the settings (transfer tiers, fixed periods) are always gross (VAT included). Spot prices published through the market APIs are always VAT-exclusive, but Kilowahti adds VAT to the prices automatically, so sensors and services always show VAT-inclusive prices.

docs.title: 3. Transfer pricing
docs.text:
Set up your network operator's transfer prices. In Kilowahti a transfer price is formed from one or more rules based on time (month, weekday and/or time of day). The rules are evaluated in priority order, and the first match wins.

You can skip this step and set up transfer prices later under Configure.

See Transfer pricing for more information about transfer prices and their rules.

docs.title: 4. Thresholds & control
docs.text:
Field Description Control max price When the price is lower than or equal to this setting, the price_acceptable binary sensor turns on Max price includes transfer Whether the price threshold compares against the total price (active price + transfer) or the active price alone Control max rank When the rank is lower than or equal to this number, the rank_acceptable binary sensor turns on Forward average window Hours ahead used for the next_hours_average sensor (1–24, in 0.25 h steps) Control factor curve Shape of the 0–1 control factor curve: Linear or Sinusoidal (see Control factor → Curve and scaling) Control factor scaling (value 1–3) Exponent applied to amplify extremes (see the link in the previous row)

Tip

Price and rank thresholds can also be adjusted without reopening the Configure view. Use the number.kilowahti_{name}_price_threshold and number.kilowahti_{name}_rank_threshold entities from the dashboard or an automation.

docs.title: 5. Optimization scores
docs.text:
A permanent Total profile is created automatically. You can link your energy meter connected to Home Assistant to it later in Kilowahti via Configure → Score profiles → Edit: Total.

Additional profiles can be added (e.g. per-device or per-circuit meters). An extra profile can, for example, track how well the price optimization of a water heater or other heating device is doing.

docs.title: 6. Advanced options
docs.text: Field Description Expose spot price arrays as attributes Writes today_prices and tomorrow_prices arrays to the spot_price sensor attributes. This is useful for graphing cards (e.g. Apex Charts) Expose total price arrays as attributes Same as above, but for the total_price sensor, with each entry broken down into energy and transfer High precision mode Shows more decimal places on price sensors and price arrays. Only needed in special cases; most setups do not need it

docs.title: Price array attributes
docs.text:
Both toggles are off by default. Values are rounded to the display precision (by default two decimals, or five in high precision mode; both have two more decimals if the display unit is €/kWh).

The arrays are not stored in the database, so they do not grow it and are not shown in history. They describe the current and next day, and are read only from the sensor's live state.

spot_price entries:

today_prices:
  - time: "2026-09-07T14:00:00+03:00"
    price: 12.34
    rank: 7

total_price entries add the breakdown, where price is the sum of the two rounded parts and rank is the total-price rank within that day (1 = cheapest). transfer is 0.0 when no transfer prices are configured:

today_prices:
  - time: "2026-09-07T14:00:00+03:00"
    energy: 8.90
    transfer: 3.44
    price: 12.34
    rank: 7

The attribute tomorrow_prices appears once tomorrow's prices have been fetched. The exception is total_price during a fixed-price period that also covers tomorrow: the prices of such periods are already known, so the array is always published when the day changes, without waiting for the spot prices.

docs.title: Updating settings
docs.text:
All settings except the initial region can be changed at any time under Configure (gear icon) without restarting Home Assistant.

To rename an instance, open Settings → Devices & Services → Kilowahti, open the entry's menu and select Reconfigure. The entry's title and unique ID follow the new name and all other settings stay as they are. If the new name is already used by another Kilowahti entry in your system, it is rejected. Renaming does not change the IDs of existing entities.

Avoid changing the display unit after setup

Changing the display unit after sensors have already recorded data may cause unit mismatches in history graphs. You may need to delete the sensors' history or update dashboard cards manually.

docs.title: Control factor
docs.text:
2026-09-082026-11-05

Most price automations are on-off switches: run the water heater, or don't. The control factor is for the other kind: devices with a dial. Heating thermostat setpoints, EV charging current, fan speeds, or the color tone or brightness of a smart lamp that reflects the spot price. Instead of asking "is it cheap enough", you get a number that says relatively how cheap right now is, and you scale the dial by it.

docs.title: The idea
docs.text:
Kilowahti ranks every slot of the day by price. The control factor turns that rank into a number between 0 and 1:

  • 1.0 — the cheapest slot of the day
  • 0.0 — the most expensive
  • anything between — proportionally in between

"Cheaper is higher" is deliberate: it makes the factor usable directly as a multiplier. Charging current becomes max_current × factor, no inversion needed.

Each factor also has a bipolar twin running from −1 to +1, for when you want a signed number: positive means cheaper than the middle of the day, negative means more expensive.

docs.title: Which control factor to use
docs.text:
Three factors, each ranking by a different price:

Sensor Ranks by Use when control_factor_price Energy price only Your grid fee is flat, or you only care about the market control_factor_total Energy plus transfer You want the real cost per kWh — usually the right one control_factor_transfer Transfer tier only You want to dodge grid peak tariffs specifically

They all share one scale, and the configured curve and scaling apply to all three.

On a fixed-price contract

During a fixed-price period every hour costs the same, so control_factor_price sits at 1.0 all day — correct, since no hour is more expensive than another. The total price factor control_factor_total still varies if your transfer tariff varies during the day.

docs.title: Curve and scaling
docs.text:
Two settings change how the rank is mapped onto the 0–1 range. Both live under Thresholds & control in the setup wizard and in Configure.

Curve — linear spreads the factor evenly across the day. sinusoidal is flat near the extremes and steep in the middle, so the cheapest few slots all score nearly 1.0, the most expensive few nearly 0.0, and the change happens across mid-range prices.

Scaling — an exponent from 1 to 3 applied to the result. Higher values push everything except the cheapest slots downward, making the factor behave more like a switch.

Values for a 24-slot day:

Rank Linear Sinusoidal Linear, scaling 2 Sinusoidal, scaling 2 1 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00 3 0.91 0.98 0.83 0.96 6 0.78 0.89 0.61 0.79 9 0.65 0.73 0.43 0.53 12 0.52 0.53 0.27 0.29 15 0.39 0.33 0.15 0.11 18 0.26 0.16 0.07 0.03 21 0.13 0.04 0.02 0.00 24 0.00 0.00 0.00 0.00

Reading across: at rank 6 — a fairly cheap hour — linear says 0.78 while sinusoidal says 0.89, treating it as nearly as good as the best. At rank 18 they diverge the other way, 0.26 against 0.16. Add scaling 2 and rank 12, the middle of the day, drops from 0.52 to 0.27.

Start with linear and scaling 1. Move to sinusoidal if your automations fidget between adjacent ranks; raise the scaling if you want the response concentrated on genuinely cheap hours.

docs.title: Using the control factor
docs.text:
The pattern is always the same: pick a desired range for your device, and place the factor inside it.

Example: Heating setpoint, 19 °C when expensive, 22 °C when cheapest:

{{ 19 + 3 * states('sensor.kilowahti_home_control_factor_total') | float(0) }}

Rank 1 gives 22.0 °C, rank 12 gives 20.6 °C, rank 24 gives 19.0 °C.

Example: EV charging current, between 6 A and 16 A:

{{ 6 + 10 * states('sensor.kilowahti_home_control_factor_total') | float(0) }}

16 A at the cheapest hour, 11.2 A mid-day, 6 A at the worst.

Both go in a number.set_value or climate.set_temperature action, triggered however you like — a time pattern every 15 minutes, or Kilowahti's own triggers. Automation examples has these written out in full.

Guard templates against missing values by setting a default

Always guard by adding | float(0) to the template, which converts the template result to a decimal number, or sets it to zero in a problem case. The control factor sensor is Unavailable until the first prices arrive, and an unguarded template throws an error on restart.

docs.title: When not to use the control factor
docs.text: The control factor answers "how cheap is now, relative to the rest of today". It says nothing about absolute price. On a day where every hour is expensive, the cheapest hour still scores 1.0. If your device absolutely must stay off when electricity is simply costly, gate it on the price threshold — binary_sensor.kilowahti_{name}_price_acceptable or the "price is acceptable" condition — and use the control factor only to modulate what happens after that gate opens.

docs.title: Entities
docs.text:
2026-03-092026-11-05

All entities are grouped under a single Kilowahti device per configured instance. Entity names use the name you set during setup (e.g. Home).

Entity IDs on your system

From 2026.11.0 Kilowahti pins its own entity IDs, so they are identical on every install no matter which language the interface is in — only the displayed names are translated into the language selected in the user's profile settings.

Installs created before 2026.11.0 keep the IDs Home Assistant generated back then, which came from the translated display name. Most are the same, but a few differ: price_rank was rank, tomorrow_available was tomorrow_s_prices_available, the setting_* diagnostics had no prefix, and a Finnish or German install got Finnish or German IDs throughout.

After upgrading, a repair under Settings → System → Repairs offers to rename them to the fixed IDs. Nothing changes until you confirm; the confirmation lists the automations, scripts, scenes and groups that use the entities (dashboards and templates are not checked), IDs you changed yourself are left alone, and the history of all IDs is kept. Any references to the old IDs, e.g. in automations or dashboard cards, must be updated by hand afterwards. If you skip the repair, check Settings → Devices & Services → Kilowahti to see your real IDs.

docs.title: Start with these
docs.text:
This page is a comprehensive reference for all of Kilowahti, and you will probably never need most of it. In a basic setup you can get very far with just five entities:

Entity What it is for sensor.kilowahti_{name}_total_price
  • What a kilowatt-hour costs you right now, everything included.
  • This number is useful, for example, in a dashboard card shown to users.
sensor.kilowahti_{name}_price_rank
  • Where the current slot sits in the day's prices by energy price, smaller is better: 1 = cheapest.
  • This number is the most useful in automations: for example, heating should not be controlled by an absolute price limit alone, because on an expensive day it could be blocked completely.
binary_sensor.kilowahti_{name}_rank_acceptable on when the rank is lower than or equal to the threshold you set number.kilowahti_{name}_rank_threshold
  • Sets the previous threshold.
  • The value can be adjusted flexibly from a dashboard or an automation without opening Kilowahti's settings, and it also changes when you edit the settings.
binary_sensor.kilowahti_{name}_tomorrow_available on when tomorrow's prices have arrived, usually in the afternoon

In addition to these, everything below is available if you need it. Kilowahti offers several sensors, some of which can achieve the very same thing with a slightly different approach and originally for a different purpose. This means broader possibilities for the user: Kilowahti is meant to be as flexible a solution as possible for different needs around electricity prices and consumption optimization.

Some of the groups below only exist when you enable them: export and solar sensors require generation enabled in Advanced options, battery sensors require, in addition to that, setting a battery capacity, and the wider rolling averages can be switched on if you want them when the selected price resolution is 15 minutes.

New to Kilowahti? The Getting started guide takes you through setting up the integration step by step from start to finish.

docs.title: Price sensors
docs.text:
All price sensors use the display unit you chose in the settings: the minor or major unit of your display currency, e.g. c/kWh or €/kWh, öre/kWh or kr/kWh.

Entity Description sensor.kilowahti_{name}_spot_price
  • Current slot's spot price including VAT
  • Attributes: price_source, plus today_prices/tomorrow_prices when price arrays are enabled
sensor.kilowahti_{name}_active_price
  • Shown as Active price. The energy price you pay: the spot price, or the contract price when a fixed period is active
  • Attributes: source (spot/fixed), period_label
sensor.kilowahti_{name}_transfer_price
  • Current transfer price, Unknown until transfer prices are configured
  • Attributes: tariff (active group and tier, e.g. "Kausisiirto, Muu aika"), plus group and tier separately
sensor.kilowahti_{name}_total_price
  • Total price, i.e. the active energy price + transfer price
  • Attributes: today_prices/tomorrow_prices when total price arrays are enabled in Advanced options
sensor.kilowahti_{name}_today_spot_average
  • Today's average spot price
sensor.kilowahti_{name}_today_spot_minimum
  • Today's lowest spot price
sensor.kilowahti_{name}_today_spot_maximum
  • Today's highest spot price
sensor.kilowahti_{name}_today_total_average
  • Today's average total price (spot + transfer)
sensor.kilowahti_{name}_today_total_minimum
  • Today's lowest total price
sensor.kilowahti_{name}_today_total_maximum
  • Today's highest total price
sensor.kilowahti_{name}_tomorrow_spot_average
  • Tomorrow's average spot price, Unavailable until tomorrow's prices are fetched
sensor.kilowahti_{name}_tomorrow_spot_minimum Tomorrow's lowest spot price; unavailable until tomorrow's prices are fetched sensor.kilowahti_{name}_tomorrow_spot_maximum Tomorrow's highest spot price; unavailable until tomorrow's prices are fetched sensor.kilowahti_{name}_tomorrow_total_average Tomorrow's average total price; unavailable until tomorrow's prices are fetched (or based on fixed period if active) sensor.kilowahti_{name}_tomorrow_total_minimum
  • Tomorrow's lowest total price
sensor.kilowahti_{name}_tomorrow_total_maximum
  • Tomorrow's highest total price
sensor.kilowahti_{name}_next_hours_average
  • Average spot price over the next N hours (configurable)
sensor.kilowahti_{name}_monthly_fixed_cost_today
  • Today's share of the monthly fixed contract cost per day in your display currency, Unavailable if the monthly fee is not configured

Spot prices are fetched every day, and the sensors update when slots change even if a fixed-price period is in use. Whether a fixed-price period is active is shown by the binary sensor fixed_price_period_active, see Binary sensors below.

docs.title: Rank sensors
docs.text:
Entity Description sensor.kilowahti_{name}_price_rank
  • Current slot's rank by the energy price you actually pay (fixed-period price when one is active, otherwise spot price), transfer price not included.
  • Normalized: 1 = cheapest, the number of slots in the day (slots_per_day) = most expensive. Read more below the table.
sensor.kilowahti_{name}_total_price_rank
  • Same, but transfer is included in the price
sensor.kilowahti_{name}_price_quartile
  • Energy price quartile 1–4 (derived from price_rank): 1 = cheapest 25 % of the day's slots
sensor.kilowahti_{name}_total_price_quartile
  • Total price quartile 1–4 (derived from total_price_rank): 1 = cheapest 25 % of the day's slots

The highest possible rank depends on price resolution

The maximum rank is 96 with 15-minute resolution and 24 with 1-hour resolution.

Ranks are normalized by price level: slots with the same price share a rank, and the cheapest price of the day is always 1 and the most expensive is always the highest possible rank. For example, if on a 15-minute resolution day the 96 slots had only two different prices, the cheaper one gets rank 1 and the more expensive one 96.

During a fixed-price period every slot costs the same, so the energy-only price_rank is 1 for the whole day, because no more expensive slot is expected during the day. Despite the fixed-price period for energy, the total price rank total_price_rank may still vary if transfer prices are defined and more than one different transfer price is active during the day.

docs.title: Control factor sensors
docs.text:
All three factors share one scale: 1.0 = cheapest, 0.0 = most expensive, with the configured shape (linear/sinusoidal) and scaling applied to each. Each of them has a bipolar version that maps the same value onto −1…+1.

Entity Range Description sensor.kilowahti_{name}_control_factor_price 0–1 Based on price_rank: the energy price, without transfer. sensor.kilowahti_{name}_control_factor_price_bipolar −1 to +1 Bipolar version of the above. sensor.kilowahti_{name}_control_factor_total 0–1 Based on total_price_rank: energy and transfer together. sensor.kilowahti_{name}_control_factor_total_bipolar −1 to +1 Bipolar version of the above. sensor.kilowahti_{name}_control_factor_transfer 0–1 Based on the rank of the transfer price among the day's transfer prices. Unknown until transfer prices are configured. sensor.kilowahti_{name}_control_factor_transfer_bipolar −1 to +1 Bipolar version of the above. Unknown until transfer prices are configured.

The transfer control factor is based on the day's different transfer prices (typically at most two or three), so it moves in larger steps than the price and total price factors, which are based on all slots. A transfer price group with only one rule, or a day spent entirely inside a fixed-price period as far as energy is concerned, gives that sensor a constant value 1: there is no reason to prefer or avoid any slot.

docs.title: Optimization sensors
docs.text:
One pair of sensors per configured optimization profile, where {profile} is the profile's name (the built-in profile's name is total, i.e. the total sum):

Entity Description sensor.kilowahti_{name}_score_{profile}_daily
  • Today's current optimization score (0–100).
  • Attribute: previous (yesterday's final score)
sensor.kilowahti_{name}_score_{profile}_monthly
  • Average of the realized daily scores of the current calendar month (0–100).
  • Attribute: previous (previous month's final score)

See the Optimization scores page to see in more detail how the scores are calculated.

docs.title: Diagnostic sensors
docs.text:
Most diagnostic sensors are disabled by default. If you want to see in more detail why or how Kilowahti behaves at any given moment, enable these sensors individually in the entity registry as needed.

Entity Description sensor.kilowahti_{name}_setting_price_threshold Configured price threshold (same unit as price sensors) sensor.kilowahti_{name}_setting_rank_threshold Configured acceptable rank threshold sensor.kilowahti_{name}_setting_price_threshold_includes_transfer Whether transfer price is included in the price threshold comparison sensor.kilowahti_{name}_setting_control_factor_shape Control factor shape (linear or sinusoidal) sensor.kilowahti_{name}_setting_forward_window Forward average window length (hours) sensor.kilowahti_{name}_setting_active_transfer_group Label of the currently active transfer group, or unavailable sensor.kilowahti_{name}_setting_active_transfer_tier Label of the currently active transfer tier, or unavailable sensor.kilowahti_{name}_setting_active_fixed_period Label of the currently active fixed-price period, or unavailable sensor.kilowahti_{name}_price_data_source Price source currently in use: kilowahti_cdn or spot_hinta (enabled by default) sensor.kilowahti_{name}_exchange_rate Daily EUR → local currency rate in use; only present when a local display currency is selected (enabled by default)

One additional diagnostic sensor per optimization profile:

Entity Description sensor.kilowahti_{name}_score_{profile}_formula The scoring formula in use in the profile: default (default) or raw (neutral)

docs.title: Number entities
docs.text:
Number entities are writable settings that can be adjusted from a dashboard or from automations with the number.set_value action. Changes take effect immediately, and no restart or reconfiguration is needed.

Entity Range Description number.kilowahti_{name}_price_threshold 0–500 in the minor unit (0–5 in the major one) Price at or below which price_acceptable turns on. The setting's unit is the same as the display unit you chose. number.kilowahti_{name}_rank_threshold 1–96 (or 1–24) Rank at or below which rank_acceptable turns on. The upper bound depends on the selected price resolution.

The initial values come from the Thresholds & control options. Changes made via these entities are persisted to the integration config, so they survive restarts and also update the values shown in the options flow.

docs.title: Rolling average sensors
docs.text:
Available only with 15-minute price resolution. Enable with the option Show next 30min, 1h and 2h average prices under Configure → Advanced options.

Entity Description sensor.kilowahti_{name}_average_price_30min Average total price for the current slot and the 30 minutes following it sensor.kilowahti_{name}_average_price_60min Average total price for the current slot and the 60 minutes following it sensor.kilowahti_{name}_average_price_120min Average total price for the current slot and the 120 minutes following it

Note that the averages are calculated from the total price (energy + transfer). If no transfer prices are configured, the average equals the plain energy price average.

docs.title: Generation & export sensors
docs.text:
The sensors in this section are available when Enable generation & export features is selected under Configure → Advanced options.

Entity Description sensor.kilowahti_{name}_export_price Current slot's feed-in price (no VAT) sensor.kilowahti_{name}_export_today_average Today's average export price sensor.kilowahti_{name}_export_today_minimum Today's lowest export price sensor.kilowahti_{name}_export_today_maximum Today's highest export price sensor.kilowahti_{name}_export_tomorrow_average Tomorrow's average export price; unavailable until fetched sensor.kilowahti_{name}_export_tomorrow_minimum Tomorrow's lowest export price sensor.kilowahti_{name}_export_tomorrow_maximum Tomorrow's highest export price sensor.kilowahti_{name}_import_export_spread Difference between current import (total) price and export price sensor.kilowahti_{name}_self_consumption_value Value of each kWh consumed from own generation (= avoided import cost) sensor.kilowahti_{name}_next_solar_window_average Average export price for the next upcoming solar production window sensor.kilowahti_{name}_arbitrage_spread_today Spread between today's cheapest and most expensive total price slots

docs.title: Battery sensors
docs.text:
The sensors in this section are available when Enable generation & export features is selected under Configure → Advanced options and, in addition, battery capacity > 0 kWh is set under Configure → Generation & export.

Entity Description sensor.kilowahti_{name}_charge_opportunity_factor How good right now is for grid charging (0.0 = worst, 1.0 = best). Always uses linear scaling — not affected by the control factor curve or scaling settings sensor.kilowahti_{name}_battery_charge_recommendation Categorical recommendation: charge_from_grid, discharge, or hold sensor.kilowahti_{name}_optimal_charge_window_start Start of the cheapest window for a full battery charge cycle sensor.kilowahti_{name}_optimal_charge_window_end End of the cheapest window for a full battery charge cycle

docs.title: Binary sensors
docs.text:
All of these sensors except price_or_rank_acceptable have counterparts as triggers and conditions, with which an automation may be easier to build.

Entity Description binary_sensor.kilowahti_{name}_price_acceptable On when current price is at or below the configured threshold binary_sensor.kilowahti_{name}_rank_acceptable On when current rank is at or below the configured threshold binary_sensor.kilowahti_{name}_price_or_rank_acceptable On when either the price or the rank condition is met binary_sensor.kilowahti_{name}_fixed_price_period_active On when a fixed-price period is currently active binary_sensor.kilowahti_{name}_tomorrow_available On when tomorrow's prices are available

The following binary sensors are available when generation is enabled:

Entity Description binary_sensor.kilowahti_{name}_export_price_acceptable On when current export price is at or above the configured export threshold

The following are available when generation is enabled and battery capacity > 0 kWh:

Entity Description binary_sensor.kilowahti_{name}_charge_from_grid_recommended On when current slot is cheap and more expensive slots follow today binary_sensor.kilowahti_{name}_discharge_to_grid_recommended On when current export price is in today's top quartile

docs.title: Why are tomorrow's prices not showing?
docs.text: Day-ahead prices are published per market in the early afternoon Central European Time, usually a little after 13:00 CET. Some markets, such as Italy, usually publish later. Kilowahti starts polling automatically at 13:00 CET by default and retries once per minute until 21:00 CET or until prices appear (both hours are configurable in Advanced options). The binary_sensor.kilowahti_{name}_tomorrow_available turns on when tomorrow's prices have arrived.

docs.title: How often does Kilowahti call the price source?
docs.text:
Kilowahti calls the price source (the Kilowahti CDN, or spot-hinta.fi as a fallback) rarely, and the calls are small. On a normal day:

  1. On HA startup, if the local cache is stale
  2. From the start of the eager-polling window (13:00 CET by default) once a minute until tomorrow's prices are published, usually no more than 15 minutes. The first successful fetch ends the polling for the day
  3. At midnight rollover, only if the tomorrow cache was empty

Regions with a non-euro currency also fetch the ECB exchange rate once a day. Sensor value updates (rank, price, etc.) come from the in-memory cache, with no network calls.

docs.title: Can I use Kilowahti without a transfer price configured?
docs.text: Yes. Transfer-related sensors (transfer_price, control_factor_transfer) show as Unknown when no transfer groups are configured. total_price then equals the active price.

docs.title: What does the control factor sensor do?
docs.text:
It turns the current price rank into a 0–1 number — 1.0 at the cheapest slot of the day, 0.0 at the most expensive — for automating devices that have a dial rather than a switch: heating setpoints, charging current, fan speed. Each control factor also has a bipolar variant on a ±1 scale.

The control factor guide covers which of the three factors to use, what the curve and scaling settings do, and how to put one into a template.

docs.title: My score sensors show no value, why?
docs.text: Score sensors only produce a value once at least one meter reading has been recorded. Make sure you have linked an energy meter entity in Configure → Score profiles → Edit: Total and that the meter has state_class: total_increasing.

docs.title: Prices look wrong — are they VAT inclusive?
docs.text: Spot prices from the API are always VAT-exclusive. Kilowahti applies VAT automatically using the rate you configured. Transfer prices and fixed-period prices are entered gross (VAT included) in Kilowahti's settings and used as-is.

docs.title: Where do prices come from?
docs.text:
Kilowahti fetches prices through an automatic source chain — there is no source setting. The primary source is the Kilowahti CDN, Kilowahti's own first-party service: it publishes day-ahead prices for all supported regions from the ENTSO-E Transparency Platform (the official European market data source) as static JSON through a European CDN (content delivery network). No account or API key is needed, and no personal data is collected.

If the CDN cannot be reached, Kilowahti falls back to the free third-party API spot-hinta.fi. Both serve the same day-ahead exchange prices, so sensor values are identical either way. Note that spot-hinta.fi only covers the Nordic and Baltic zones; in other regions the Kilowahti CDN is the only source, so there is no fallback (options are being looked at, promise).

The diagnostic sensor price_data_source shows which source is currently in use.

docs.title: What happens if the price sources are unavailable?
docs.text: Kilowahti continues serving data from its local cache. As long as the cache holds valid slots for the current day, all sensors update normally — no network call is needed for each update. If the cache is empty or stale and every source in the chain fails, price sensors will become unavailable. It is worth testing your automations to ensure they behave safely (fail-closed) when sensors are unavailable.

docs.title: How does local currency display work?
docs.text: Regions outside the eurozone can show all prices in the local billing currency (see Configuration). Electricity market trading always happens in EUR, and Kilowahti converts prices with a daily exchange rate. By default the ECB reference rate is used, or alternatively a manual rate you enter. The rate is frozen for the whole day, so already published slot prices never shift mid-day. Switching between EUR and local currency converts your entered prices (commission, transfer tiers, fixed periods, thresholds) automatically. Note that Home Assistant long-term statistics recorded before a currency switch keep their old unit and are not converted.

docs.title: Can I have multiple Kilowahti instances?
docs.text: Yes. Add more entries to the Kilowahti integration with different names and regions (Settings → Devices & Services → Kilowahti → Add entry). Service calls that don't specify config_entry_id work automatically when only one instance is configured.

docs.title: Fixed-price periods
docs.text:
2026-03-092026-11-05

Fixed-price periods let you define date ranges where a flat contract price replaces the spot price. This is useful if you have a fixed-price electricity contract, or a price locked in on a spot contract, for part of the year, or continuously if your entire contract is fixed-rate.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
When a fixed period is active:

  • sensor.kilowahti_{name}_active_price (shown as Active price) returns the fixed price instead of the spot price
  • sensor.kilowahti_{name}_total_price = fixed price + transfer price
  • binary_sensor.kilowahti_{name}_fixed_price_period_active is on
  • The price_acceptable binary sensor compares against the fixed price
  • sensor.kilowahti_{name}_price_rank reads 1 for every slot, and control_factor_price a constant 1.0 — with one price all day, no hour is better than another. total_price_rank still separates the hours if your transfer tariff has tiers

The spot price sensor continues to show the live spot price regardless, so you can still see what the market is doing.

docs.title: Managing periods
docs.text:
Periods can be managed via Configure → Fixed-price periods or using service calls.

Note

Periods cannot overlap. The price is entered gross (VAT included) and used as-is.

docs.title: Via the UI
docs.text: Configure → Fixed-price periods → ➕ Add period

docs.title: Via service calls
docs.text:
# Add a period
action: kilowahti.add_fixed_period
data:
  label: "Q1 2026 fixation"
  start_date: "2026-01-01"
  end_date: "2026-03-31"
  price: 8.5

# List all periods (to get IDs)
action: kilowahti.list_fixed_periods
data: {}

# Remove a period
action: kilowahti.remove_fixed_period
data:
  period_id: "3f4a1b2c-..."

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
2026-09-082026-11-05

This page walks through a first setup end to end: install, answer the wizard, check that prices arrived, and build one automation. Setup takes about ten minutes, and every optional feature is skipped. You can easily add features later by editing the settings.

If you would rather go through the settings yourself without the instructions on this page, you can read about all of them on the Configuration page.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need to know two things:

  • Your bidding zone. In many countries this is the area your electricity is billed in, not just the country: for example Sweden has four, Norway five, Italy seven. All the zones are listed on the supported regions page. If you are unsure, the zone is usually named on your electricity bill or on your supplier's website.
  • What kind of electricity contract you have (spot or fixed price). Kilowahti works with both. Start with the spot setup below anyway, and handle a fixed-price contract by adding a fixed-price period afterwards. (Even if a fixed contract is valid indefinitely, in Kilowahti it is still a "period".)

You do not need an API key, an account, or any other integration. Kilowahti started partly because the existing integrations struggled with the switch to 15-minute pricing. Prices are always fetched into Kilowahti automatically, and usually reach your system within a minute or two of their Europe-wide publication.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
Follow the Installation instructions. In short, depending on your Home Assistant version:

  • Home Assistant version 2026.11 and newer: Settings → Marketplace → search Kilowahti → Install.
  • Older Home Assistant versions: HACS → search Kilowahti → Download → restart Home Assistant.

docs.title: 2. Run the wizard
docs.text:
Before Home Assistant version 2026.11 the setup wizard has to be started manually: Settings → Devices & Services → Add Integration → Kilowahti

The wizard has six steps, or seven if your region bills in a local currency. For a first setup, you only need to decide these:

Step What to do first time Basic settings
  • Enter a short name (e.g. Home) — the chosen name becomes part of every entity ID.
  • Pick your bidding zone.
  • Leave resolution at 15 minutes unless your contract still bills hourly.
Currency
  • This step is only shown outside the eurozone.
  • Pick your local currency and leave the exchange rate on automatic.
VAT & electricity tax
  • Taxes are pre-filled based on the selected bidding zone and normally do not need changing at this stage.
  • A margin defined in a spot contract is entered in the Commission field.
Transfer pricing
  • Skip it for now.
  • Transfer prices can be added later, and the basic functionality does not suffer if none are set.
Thresholds & control
  • Accept the defaults at this stage.
Optimization scores
  • Skip it for now.
  • A Total profile is created automatically, and a meter can be attached to it later.
Advanced options
  • Leave everything off.

That's it, Kilowahti's entities appear right after setup.

About the default thresholds

The defaults Kilowahti uses are meant as a starting point for your own settings, and are not a real recommendation. The default price threshold is 20 c/kWh and the rank threshold 24. With 15-minute prices a rank threshold of 24 means "the cheapest 24 of today's 96 slots", i.e. a total of the cheapest six hours of the day (24 × 15 min = 360 min = 6 h). Both can be adjusted later from a dashboard, see step 5.

docs.title: 3. Check that it worked
docs.text:
Go to Settings → Devices & Services → Kilowahti and open the instance the integration created, under the name you set (e.g. Kilowahti Home). All of Kilowahti's entities live there. Look for these:

Entity What you should see sensor.kilowahti_{name}_spot_price The market price for right now sensor.kilowahti_{name}_total_price What you actually pay per kWh, VAT and grid fees included sensor.kilowahti_{name}_price_rank Where this slot ranks in today's prices — 1 is the cheapest of the day binary_sensor.kilowahti_{name}_rank_acceptable on when the current slot is at or below your rank threshold sensor.kilowahti_{name}_price_data_source Which price source is being used

Replace {name} with the name you entered, lowercased, e.g. sensor.kilowahti_home_price_data_source.

Tomorrow's prices may not be visible yet, and that is normal. The European electricity market publishes the prices in the early afternoon, but the exact time varies. Kilowahti starts fetching prices at 13:00 Central European Time and gets them from its own content delivery network (CDN) with very little delay after publication. Until the updated prices have been received, every tomorrow_* sensor reads Unknown.

docs.title: 4. Build your first automation
docs.text:
An example of an easy and simple automation: when the price is among the lowest of the current day, turn on a smart light, heat water, charge a car, or run a dishwasher.

  1. Settings → Automations & scenes → Add automation → Create new automation
  2. Add trigger → search rank → select Rank became acceptable
  3. Add action → here choose any action you want to switch on
  4. Save

Your automation is ready. It runs whenever the slot changes (every 15 or 60 minutes) and the slot that has started falls in the cheapest part of the day, as defined by the rank threshold.

If you want to switch the device off again automatically, you can make a second automation with the Rank no longer acceptable trigger.

Triggers and conditions lists all the triggers and conditions you can use to start an automation. If the triggers alone are not enough for your needs, Automation examples shows more versatile implementations.

docs.title: 5. Tune the thresholds later
docs.text:
You do not need to reopen the setup wizard to change how aggressive your automations are. Two entities control it, and both can be added to a dashboard to make them editable:

  • number.kilowahti_{name}_price_threshold
  • number.kilowahti_{name}_rank_threshold

When you adjust their values, every binary sensor, trigger and condition based on them follows immediately.

A minimal dashboard card to see the essentials together:

type: entities
title: Electricity
entities:
  - entity: sensor.kilowahti_{name}_total_price
  - entity: sensor.kilowahti_{name}_price_rank
  - entity: binary_sensor.kilowahti_{name}_rank_acceptable
  - entity: number.kilowahti_{name}_rank_threshold

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
As your needs grow, have a look at these. The order does not matter, nothing depends on the others:

  • Transfer pricing Enter your grid operator's transfer prices into Kilowahti so total_price reflects your real cost. Worth doing; grid fees are often a third of the bill.
  • Fixed-price periods If you have a fixed-price contract, or a price locked in on a spot contract, tell Kilowahti its price and validity period. Price sensors switch to your contract price for those days.
  • Optimization scores Point Kilowahti to the entity in Home Assistant of an energy meter that measures all your consumption (e.g. a HomeWizard P1 plugged into the HAN port of a newer electricity meter, or a Shelly installed by an electrician), and get a daily/monthly score of 0–100 that tells how well your consumption was directed to cheap hours.
  • Entities Full list of Kilowahti's entities, including export, battery and solar sensors that appear once the feature has been enabled in Advanced options.
  • Frequently asked questions (FAQ) Answers to questions on your mind, such as why tomorrow's prices are missing, why your prices differ from your bills, what the control factor is for, and many more.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
2026-09-082026-11-05

The glossary explains in plain language the terms used elsewhere in these docs.

docs.title: Prices and the market
docs.text:
Bidding zone (also price area, price region) The area your electricity price is set for. Not the same as a country: Sweden has four zones, Norway five, Italy seven, while Germany and Luxembourg share one. Your bill or your supplier's information usually names yours. The supported regions page lists all 43 zones.

Day-ahead price The wholesale price set one day in advance in an auction, per slot, per bidding zone. This is what "spot price" means in a household context: tomorrow's prices are decided in the early afternoon today and do not change afterwards.

Spot price In Kilowahti, the market price for a slot with your VAT and supplier commission applied. The raw market price arrives in Kilowahti excluding VAT; the spot_price sensor always shows it to you including VAT.

Slot The unit of time prices are set for: 15 minutes (96 per day) or 1 hour (24 per day), depending on your configuration. Prices are constant within a slot and can change whenever the slot changes.

Resolution The length of the slot you use: 15 minutes or one hour. Choose according to the metering interval of your electricity contract.

Commission (also margin) The per-kWh amount your supplier adds on top of the spot price. Entered gross, VAT included.

Transfer price (also grid fee, network fee, distribution) The price your grid operator charges for delivering the electricity to you, separate from what you pay your supplier for the energy itself. Often a third or more of the total electricity cost.

Tier A time-based rule inside a transfer price group: a price per kWh plus when it applies (months, weekdays, hours). The first matching tier by priority wins.

Fixed-price period A time period during which a fixed contract price replaces the spot price. See fixed-price periods.

Gross / net Gross means VAT included, net means excluding. Everything you type into Kilowahti is gross; everything arriving from the market is net, and VAT is added for you automatically.

docs.title: Other Kilowahti terms
docs.text:
Energy price (also electricity price) What you pay per kWh for the electricity itself: the spot price on a spot contract, your contract rate during a fixed-price period. Transfer excluded.

Total price Energy price plus transfer price. The number that most closely matches your bill.

Rank Where the current slot sits among the same day's slots, starting from the cheapest. 1 is the cheapest of the day; the rank of the most expensive price is always the number of slots (24 or 96, depending on resolution). Slots that cost the same share a rank, so during a fixed-price period the energy price rank of every slot is 1. The total price rank is still affected by the transfer price during a fixed-price period, so it can vary even if the energy price stays the same all day.

Quartile The same idea in four coarser buckets, usually written Q1-Q4. Q1 = cheapest quarter of the day, Q4 = most expensive.

Control factor The rank expressed as a number between 0 and 1, with 1.0 at the cheapest and 0.0 at the most expensive. Made for feeding into automations that have a dial rather than a switch: charging current, heating setpoint, fan speed. See the control factor guide.

Bipolar The same value on a −1 to +1 scale instead of 0 to 1. Use it when you want a signed number that tells whether the price is cheaper or more expensive than usual.

Threshold Your definition of "cheap enough". There are two: a price threshold in currency per kWh, and a rank threshold as a position in the day. Both drive binary sensors, triggers, and conditions, and both can be adjusted straight from a dashboard in everyday use.

Score A 0–100 measure of how well your actual consumption was directed to the day's cheap slots. See optimization scores.

Eager polling The afternoon time window in which Kilowahti keeps checking for tomorrow's prices until they appear.

docs.title: Home Assistant terms
docs.text:
Entity One value in Home Assistant, e.g. sensor.kilowahti_home_total_price. Kilowahti creates a set of them for each configured entry.

Binary sensor An entity whose state is always either on or off, for example "the price is acceptable right now".

Number entity A value you can set from the interface as well as read. Kilowahti's thresholds are number entities, so you can change them from a dashboard once you have added them to a card.

Trigger / condition A trigger starts an automation when something happens, and a condition decides whether the triggered automation may run or is stopped right away. Kilowahti provides its own of both.

Recorder The part of Home Assistant that writes entity values to the database, forming their raw history. Kilowahti's price arrays are deliberately kept out of it.

Long-term statistics The long-lived hourly summaries Home Assistant keeps for numeric entities. Hourly statistics are stored separately from the raw history, which Home Assistant prunes over time.

docs.title: Optimization scores
docs.text:
2026-03-092026-11-05

Kilowahti's optimization scores tell how well your electricity consumption is directed to cheap slots. A score of 100 means consumption has concentrated in the cheapest slots. A score near 0 means consumption falls mostly on the most expensive slots.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Each day is divided into four quartiles by the slot's price rank (which depends on the selected price resolution):

Quartile Rank range (15-min) Rank range (1-hour) Meaning Q1 1–24 1–6 Cheapest 25% of slots Q2 25–48 7–12 Q3 49–72 13–18 Q4 73–96 19–24 Most expensive 25%

Kilowahti tracks energy consumption (from your linked meter entities) slot by slot and accumulates totals per quartile throughout the day.

docs.title: Formulas
docs.text: Two scoring formulas are available per profile. Both give a full 100 points when all consumption is in the first quartile, but the default formula makes that easier to reach. You can select the formula when you add or edit a profile.

docs.title: Default formula
docs.text:
raw = (Q1×3 + Q2×2 + Q3×1) / (Total×3) × 100
score = clamp((raw − 30) / 53.3 × 100, 0, 100)
Scenario Score All consumption in Q1 100 Equal split between Q1 and Q2 100 Perfectly uniform across all quartiles ~38 All consumption in Q3 ~6 All consumption in Q4 0

The formula is weighted so that random, unoptimized consumption scores around 38 instead of an average 50. This leaves more room at the top end to reward deliberate shifting to cheap slots. On the other hand, full points only need all consumption to be in the cheapest half of the day's slots, with at least half of it in the first quartile. To get above 50 points with this formula, consumption has to be moved from the day's most expensive slots to cheaper ones. That is why this is Kilowahti's default formula.

docs.title: Raw formula
docs.text:
score = clamp((Q1×3 + Q2×2 + Q3×1) / (Total×3) × 100, 0, 100)
Scenario Score All consumption in Q1 100 Equal split between Q1 and Q2 ~83 Perfectly uniform across all quartiles 50 All consumption in Q3 ~33 All consumption in Q4 0

Uses a neutral baseline: perfectly uniform consumption scores exactly 50. Easier to interpret at a glance — below 50 means worse than random, above 50 means better. On the other hand, with this formula it is easier to settle for unoptimized consumption, because changes in consumption cause smaller changes in the score: optimizing moves the score less toward "better".

docs.title: Daily and monthly scores
docs.text:
• Daily score (score_{profile}_daily) changes through the day as the price slot changes. Resets at midnight. Exposes a previous attribute with yesterday's final score.
  • Monthly score (score_{profile}_monthly) is the average of the realized daily scores of the current calendar month (so not a rolling 30-day window). Updated each midnight. Exposes a previous attribute with the previous calendar month's final score.

Score sensors refresh at each price slot boundary (every 15 or 60 minutes depending on your resolution setting), not on every individual meter reading.

Daily scores are stored for 90 days. The last two completed calendar-month scores are stored separately and available via the previous attribute even after the 90-day history window has passed.

docs.title: Setting up score profiles
docs.text:
1. Go to Settings → Devices & Services → Kilowahti → Configure → Score profiles
  2. Click ✎ Edit next to the Total profile
  3. Select ➕ Add meter(s) and pick your main grid import meter
  4. Select ⚙ Formula to choose a scoring formula (Default or Raw)
  5. Click ← Back, then ✓ Save & close

You can also add other profiles if you track individual circuits or devices with their own energy meters. Each profile can have its own formula.

The meter entity's value must be increasing

The energy meter entity must have state_class: total_increasing. This is standard for energy meters in Home Assistant (e.g. sensor.electricity_meter_energy).

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
2026-03-092026-11-05

All services are registered under the kilowahti domain. Every service takes an optional config_entry_id field that says which Kilowahti instance to use. When only one instance is configured it can be omitted. With several instances it is required: a call without it fails with a validation error, so the examples below leave it out for brevity but need it added in a multi-instance setup.

Invalid calls (no Kilowahti entry configured, unknown config_entry_id or period id, an invalid or overlapping fixed period) fail with a validation error that Home Assistant shows in the UI and in automation traces. Automations that catch the error should catch ServiceValidationError.

docs.title: Price queries
docs.text: All price queries accept a formatted parameter (default true), which rounds prices to your display precision and converts them to your display unit. When false, prices come back at full precision in the minor unit of your display currency (c/kWh, öre/kWh, …).

docs.title: kilowahti.get_active_prices
docs.text:
Returns all price slots for today and tomorrow (default), or a custom time range. Each slot includes the active price (spot, or your contract rate during a fixed-price period) and the total price (active price + transfer).

action: kilowahti.get_active_prices
data: {}

action: kilowahti.get_active_prices
data:
  start: "2026-03-10T00:00:00"
  end: "2026-03-10T23:59:59"
  formatted: false

Response (shortened for the example; the full response has one element for each slot in the time range): 

{
  "unit": "c/kWh",
  "price_periods": [
    {
      "time": "2026-03-10T00:00:00+02:00",
      "price": 4.32,
      "total_price": 6.87,
      "rank": 3,
      "is_fixed": false
    },
    {
      "time": "2026-03-10T00:15:00+02:00",
      "price": 4.32,
      "total_price": 6.87,
      "rank": 3,
      "is_fixed": false
    },
    "..."
  ]
}

docs.title: kilowahti.get_prices
docs.text:
Returns raw spot price slots for a time range. Prices are spot-only (with VAT and commission applied) — fixed-price periods and transfer are not included in these prices. The time of each slot in the response is in UTC.

action: kilowahti.get_prices
data:
  start: "2026-03-10T00:00:00"
  end: "2026-03-10T23:59:59"

docs.title: kilowahti.cheapest_hours
docs.text:
Within a time range, based on total price (spot or fixed-period rate plus transfer), finds the cheapest consecutive window of the desired length.

action: kilowahti.cheapest_hours
data:
  start: "2026-03-10T18:00:00"
  end: "2026-03-11T08:00:00"
  hours: 3
  reverse: false  # optional, default: false

Find the latest window with reverse

Set reverse: true to return the latest cheapest window when there are ties (useful for "charge the battery at a lower price before prices rise" automations, or when searching at night for the latest valid heating window before prices rise in the morning). Default false returns the earliest possible window.

Response: 

{
  "start": "2026-03-10T20:00:00+00:00",
  "end": "2026-03-10T22:45:00+00:00",
  "average_price": 3.21,
  "unit": "c/kWh",
  "price_periods": [...]
}

start and end are in UTC. end is the start time of the window's last slot, not the moment the window finishes: above, the last of the twelve 15-minute slots starts at 22:45 UTC and ends at 23:00. The time values in price_periods are UTC too.

Scheduling appliances at the cheapest time

Call this service once per day after tomorrow's prices arrive, store the result in an input_datetime helper, and trigger your appliance from that. See Automation examples → Schedule appliance at cheapest upcoming window for a complete example.

docs.title: kilowahti.average_price
docs.text:
Returns aggregate price statistics for a time range, using the spot price with VAT and commission applied. Fixed-price periods and transfer are not included in these prices.

action: kilowahti.average_price
data:
  start: "2026-03-10T00:00:00"
  end: "2026-03-10T23:59:59"

Response: 

{
  "average_price": 5.14,
  "min_price": 1.23,
  "max_price": 12.87,
  "unit": "c/kWh",
  "slot_count": 96
}

docs.title: Generation & export
docs.text: These services require generation to be enabled in configuration.

docs.title: kilowahti.get_export_prices
docs.text:
Returns export price slots for a time range, using the configured export pricing mode (spot-linked or fixed rate).

action: kilowahti.get_export_prices
data:
  start: "2026-03-10T00:00:00"
  end: "2026-03-10T23:59:59"

Response: 

{
  "unit": "c/kWh",
  "price_periods": [
    {
      "time": "2026-03-10T00:00:00+02:00",
      "export_price": 3.00
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: kilowahti.best_export_hours
docs.text:
Finds the most profitable consecutive window for grid export within a time range, using export price.

action: kilowahti.best_export_hours
data:
  start: "2026-03-10T08:00:00"
  end: "2026-03-10T20:00:00"
  hours: 2

Response: 

{
  "start": "2026-03-10T12:00:00+00:00",
  "end": "2026-03-10T13:45:00+00:00",
  "average_export_price": 8.45,
  "unit": "c/kWh",
  "price_periods": [...]
}

start and end are in UTC, and end is the start time of the window's last slot (above, the last of eight 15-minute slots starts at 13:45 UTC and ends at 14:00). The time values in price_periods are in local time.

docs.title: kilowahti.generation_schedule
docs.text:
Takes an hourly solar generation forecast and returns a recommended action for each slot.

action: kilowahti.generation_schedule
data:
  forecast:
    - time: "2026-03-10T10:00:00"
      kwh: 2.5
    - time: "2026-03-10T11:00:00"
      kwh: 3.1

Response: 

{
  "schedule": [
    {
      "time": "2026-03-10T10:00:00+02:00",
      "kwh": 2.5,
      "action": "self_consume",
      "export_price": 3.20,
      "self_consumption_value": 7.85
    }
  ]
}

Possible action values: export, self_consume and idle. The recommendation is export when the export price is at least as high as the self-consumption value (spot price plus transfer), otherwise self_consume if the slot has forecast generation, otherwise idle.

docs.title: kilowahti.add_fixed_period
docs.text:
Adds a fixed-price contract period. Periods cannot overlap.

action: kilowahti.add_fixed_period
data:
  label: "Winter fixation"
  start_date: "2026-01-01"
  end_date: "2026-03-31"
  price: 8.5

Always enter prices including VAT

price is entered gross (VAT included). It is used as-is, and VAT is not added on top.
