docs.title: Transfer pricing
docs.text:
2026-03-092026-11-05

This is how you set up your network operator's transfer prices in Kilowahti so that they are included in price calculations and sensors.

docs.title: Groups and tiers
docs.text:
Transfer pricing is organised into groups that correspond to the different transfer products of network operators, each containing one or more tiers — a tier is a rule that activates when its conditions are met. Only one group is active at a time — this lets you store multiple contracts (e.g. seasonal or time-of-use) and switch between them without re-entering data. (Remember to always check that the prices you entered earlier are still up to date.)

A group has a name (e.g. Aikasiirto or Yösiirto) and the monthly fee of that transfer product or connection.

Each tier in a group has a transfer price per kWh and the conditions for when it applies:

Field Description Price In your display unit, gross (VAT included) Months active Which months this tier applies Weekdays active Which days of the week Start / end time Sets the hour range during which the condition is met (start inclusive, end exclusive: 6–22 covers 6:00–21:59) Priority The order in which tiers are checked — see below

docs.title: How priority works
docs.text:
Tiers are checked in ascending priority order, i.e. the smallest number first, and the first one that matches wins. A smaller priority number therefore means a tier is checked earlier than a larger one, so priority 1 beats priority 2.

The practical pattern is: describe your restricted rates explicitly with tiers that have small priority numbers, and give the fallback rate the largest number so that it only applies when no earlier tier matched.

Always end with a catch-all

Give your base rate no time restrictions — all months, all weekdays, hours 0 to 24 — and the highest priority number in the group. It then acts as a fallback at the bottom, guaranteeing that every hour of the year has a transfer price. Without one, hours matching no tier have no transfer price at all.

docs.title: Viewing and editing tiers
docs.text:
Open Configure → Transfer pricing and select a group. The group screen lists every tier it holds — price, months, weekdays, hour range, and priority — in evaluation order.

Selecting ✎ Edit tier opens the tier with all of its current values filled in. Change any field and confirm to save, or tick Remove this tier to delete it.

docs.title: Effect on sensors and binary sensors
docs.text:
When a transfer group is active:

  • sensor.kilowahti_{name}_transfer_price shows the current tier's price. Its tariff attribute names the group and tier in use, e.g. Kausisiirto, Muu aika, and both are also available in their own attributes, group and tier
  • sensor.kilowahti_{name}_total_price becomes the active price plus the transfer price
  • sensor.kilowahti_{name}_control_factor_transfer rates the current tier against the other tiers occurring today: 1.0 = cheapest tier, 0.0 = most expensive, on the same scale as the other control factors. A group with only one tier in play sits at a constant 1.0. There is a bipolar variant running from −1 to +1
  • sensor.kilowahti_{name}_total_price_rank and control_factor_total take the transfer price into account; the plain price_rank and control_factor_price do not
  • The price_acceptable binary sensor can optionally include the transfer price in its comparison (configured via Max price includes transfer)

Until a transfer group is configured, transfer_price and control_factor_transfer read unknown rather than zero — Kilowahti does not pretend the grid is free.

docs.title: Example: Finnish Yleissiirto (flat rate)
docs.text:
Yleissiirto is a single-rate tariff with no time restrictions — the same price applies around the clock, every day of the year. It requires only one tier.

Step-by-step setup

  1. Go to Settings → Devices & Services → Kilowahti → Configure → Transfer pricing
  2. Select ➕ Add group, enter the name Yleissiirto, enter your operator's monthly fee, and save
  3. Select ⚙ Manage: Yleissiirto from the list

  4. Select ➕ Add tier and fill in the single rate:

    Field Value Tier name Yleissiirto Price (your operator's rate per kWh, incl. VAT) Months active (all months) Weekdays active (all days) Start time 0 End time 24 Priority 1

  5. Select ← Back, then ✓ Save & close

  6. To activate, open the group again and choose Set as active group

docs.title: Example: Finnish Aikasiirto (day/night tariff)
docs.text:
Aikasiirto is a two-rate tariff based on time of day: a higher day rate and a lower night rate. The boundary is typically 22:00–07:00, but check your operator's contract for the exact hours.

Rate When Päivä (day) 07:00–22:00, every day Yö (night) 22:00–07:00, every day

Because Kilowahti evaluates tiers in ascending priority order and stops at the first match, give the more restricted rate (day, i.e. one continuous period within the same day) the smaller number and let the night rate act as the base tier behind it.

Step-by-step setup

  1. Go to Settings → Devices & Services → Kilowahti → Configure → Transfer pricing
  2. Select ➕ Add group, enter the name Aikasiirto, enter the transfer product's monthly fee, and save
  3. Select ⚙ Manage: Aikasiirto from the list

  4. Select ➕ Add tier and fill in the day rate:

    Field Value Tier name Päivä Price (your operator's day rate per kWh, incl. VAT) Months active (all months) Weekdays active (all days) Start time 7 End time 22 Priority 1

  5. Select ➕ Add tier again and fill in the night catch-all:

    Field Value Tier name Yö Price (your operator's night rate per kWh, incl. VAT) Months active (all months) Weekdays active (all days) Start time 0 End time 24 Priority 2

    Start 0 and end 24 means the tier covers the full day — this is intentional for a catch-all. Its larger priority number means it is only reached when no earlier tier matched.

  6. Select ← Back, then ✓ Save & close

  7. To activate, open the group again and choose Set as active group

The day tier (priority 1) matches between 07:00–22:00. Outside those hours the night tier (priority 2) catches everything.

docs.title: Example: Finnish Kausisiirto (seasonal tariff)
docs.text:
Finnish network operators commonly offer a kausisiirto (seasonal transfer) tariff with two rates:

Rate When Talviarkipäivä (peak) November–March, Mon–Sat, 06:00–22:00 (or 07:00–22:00) Muu aika (off-peak) Everything else (Apr–Oct, winter Sundays, nights)

Same priority approach as Aikasiirto above — the peak rate is described explicitly with priority 1, and the off-peak tier catches everything else with priority 2.

Step-by-step setup

  1. Go to Settings → Devices & Services → Kilowahti → Configure → Transfer pricing
  2. Select ➕ Add group, enter the name Kausisiirto, enter the transfer product's monthly fee, and save
  3. Select ⚙ Manage: Kausisiirto from the list

  4. Select ➕ Add tier and fill in the peak rate:

    Field Value Tier name Talviarkipäivä Price (your operator's peak rate per kWh, incl. VAT) Months active November, December, January, February, March Weekdays active Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday Start time 6 End time 22 Priority 1

  5. Select ➕ Add tier again and fill in the off-peak catch-all:

    Field Value Tier name Muu aika Price (your operator's off-peak rate per kWh, incl. VAT) Months active (all months) Weekdays active (all days) Start time 0 End time 24 Priority 2

    Start 0 and end 24 means the tier covers the full day — this is intentional for a catch-all. Its larger priority number means it is only reached when no earlier tier matched.

  6. Select ← Back, then ✓ Save & close

  7. To activate, open the group again and choose Set as active group

The peak tier (priority 1) matches first whenever it is November–March, a weekday (Mon–Sat), and between 06:00–22:00. All other times fall through to the off-peak tier (priority 2).

docs.title: Switching groups
docs.text:
Go to Configure → Transfer pricing, select a group, and choose Set as active group. Only one group is active at a time, and switching takes effect immediately — no restart, no reload.

Edits to the active group's tiers also apply immediately.

docs.title: Triggers and conditions
docs.text:
2026-09-082026-11-05

Kilowahti ships its own automation triggers and conditions. They appear in the Home Assistant automation editor alongside the built-in ones, so you can build a price-aware automation without picking entities, writing templates, or knowing which sensor holds which number.

They are the easiest starting point for a first automation. The automation examples show the same ideas built from entities instead, which is what you need for anything the triggers do not cover.

docs.title: Adding one in the UI
docs.text:
1. Settings → Automations & scenes → Create automation → Create new automation
  2. Add trigger → search by the trigger's name, e.g. rank, price or cheapest
  3. Pick a trigger, then add your action

Conditions work the same way under Add condition.

Search by name, not by Kilowahti

The picker searches trigger and condition names in your interface language. Searching for Kilowahti only finds the device and its entities, not the triggers. With several Kilowahti entries, add a target to say which one the trigger watches — see below.

If you have several Kilowahti entries set up (one per region or site), the trigger has an Add target button — use it to pick that entry's device. With several entries, a trigger or condition without a target does nothing: the trigger never fires and the condition never passes. With a single entry you can leave the target out and it will be used automatically.

docs.title: Triggers
docs.text: Trigger Fires when Price became acceptable The current price drops to or below your price threshold Price no longer acceptable The current price rises above your price threshold Rank became acceptable The current slot's rank drops to or below your rank threshold Rank no longer acceptable The current slot's rank rises above your rank threshold Became cheapest slot The current slot becomes the cheapest of the day by total price Fixed period started A fixed-price period becomes active Fixed period ended A fixed-price period stops being active Tomorrow's prices available Tomorrow's prices have been fetched, usually in the afternoon

docs.title: Conditions
docs.text:
Condition Passes when Price is acceptable The current price is at or below your price threshold Rank is acceptable The current slot's rank is at or below your rank threshold Price is lowest today The current slot is the cheapest of the day by total price Fixed period active A fixed-price period is currently active Tomorrow's prices available Tomorrow's prices have been fetched

A condition that cannot be evaluated — no price data yet, or a target that matches no Kilowahti entry — does not pass. Automations gated on it simply do not run.

docs.title: Things worth knowing
docs.text:
Triggers fire on the change, not while it lasts. "Price became acceptable" fires once, at the moment the price crosses your threshold. It does not fire again every slot while the price stays low. To act on a state that is already true, use a condition, or the matching binary sensor.

Restarting or reloading does not fire them. Each trigger reads the current situation when it starts and treats that as its baseline, so reloading automations in the middle of a cheap hour does not produce a spurious run.

Thresholds are live. The price and rank thresholds come from your configuration, and both are also exposed as number entities you can change from a dashboard or an automation. Change a threshold and the triggers use the new value immediately — no reload.

Price includes transfer only if you asked for it. The price threshold compares against the energy price by default, or energy plus transfer when Price threshold includes transfer is enabled in the options.

"Cheapest slot" always includes transfer. "Became cheapest slot" and "Price is lowest today" rank by the total price you pay, energy plus transfer. On a day where several slots share the cheapest total price, all of them count as cheapest.

On a fixed-price contract, rank stops discriminating. Rank follows the energy price you actually pay. During a fixed-price period every hour costs the same, so every slot ranks 1, "Rank is acceptable" always passes, and "Rank became acceptable" never fires — there is no cheaper hour to move to. Use "Price is lowest today" or "Became cheapest slot" if you still want the transfer-cheap hours on such a day.

docs.title: In YAML
docs.text:
The UI is the easier route, but the same triggers and conditions can be written by hand:

alias: Heat water when the price drops
triggers:
  - trigger: kilowahti.price_became_acceptable
conditions:
  - condition: kilowahti.tomorrow_available
actions:
  - action: switch.turn_on
    target:
      entity_id: switch.water_heater

With more than one Kilowahti entry, name the one you mean:

triggers:
  - trigger: kilowahti.rank_became_acceptable
    target:
      device_id: 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

Trigger keys are kilowahti. followed by the name in snake_case: price_became_acceptable, price_no_longer_acceptable, rank_became_acceptable, rank_no_longer_acceptable, became_cheapest_slot, fixed_period_started, fixed_period_ended, tomorrow_prices_available. Condition keys follow the same pattern: price_is_acceptable, rank_is_acceptable, price_is_lowest_today, fixed_period_active, tomorrow_available.

docs.title: When to use the binary sensors instead
docs.text:
The binary sensors cover the same ground as states rather than events, which makes them the better choice when you want to:

  • see the current situation on a dashboard, or its history in a graph
  • combine several conditions in one template
  • start an automation from a state that is already true, without waiting for the next change

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
2026-09-082026-11-05

Symptoms first. If your problem is "how do I make Kilowahti do X", see How do I…? instead.

docs.title: No prices at all
docs.text:
If spot_price and everything derived from it read unknown or unavailable:

  • Right after setup, give Kilowahti a moment. Prices are fetched during setup; the entities appear before the first fetch completes.
  • Check the source. sensor.kilowahti_{name}_price_data_source names the source currently serving you. If it is unavailable, no source answered.
  • Check outbound access. Kilowahti needs HTTPS to cdn.kilowahti.fi and, as fallback, api.spot-hinta.fi. A restrictive DNS filter or firewall on the Home Assistant host may block both.
  • Look in the log. Settings → System → Logs, filter for kilowahti. A failing source logs the reason why it failed.

Kilowahti caches prices locally, so a temporary outage does not empty your sensors — you keep the day you already have.

docs.title: A "Using a fallback price source" repair appears
docs.text: Kilowahti has served your region from a secondary price source for over 24 hours, which usually means the primary source is having an outage. Prices stay correct; the repair clears itself once the primary source answers again, and no action is needed. If it persists for days, check outbound access as described under No prices at all and look for the failure reason in the log.

docs.title: Tomorrow's prices are missing
docs.text:
This is normal for most of the day. The European electricity market's day-ahead auction publishes results in the early afternoon, but the exact time varies. Kilowahti begins looking at 13:00 CET and keeps trying until they appear or 21:00 CET passes. Most of the time the prices have been fetched into Home Assistant by 13:15 CET.

binary_sensor.kilowahti_{name}_tomorrow_available turns on when they arrive. Until then every tomorrow_* sensor reads unknown, and that is the intended value — not an error.

Some price areas publish later than others, for example Italy is regularly among the last.

docs.title: Prices do not match my bill
docs.text:
Work through it in this order:

  1. VAT Market prices arrive without VAT, and Kilowahti adds the rate you configured. Check it against your bill.
  2. Supplier margin If your contract adds a per-kWh commission, enter it in the settings, because it is not in the market price.
  3. Transfer prices The energy price sensor spot_price never includes transfer. Compare your bill against total_price and make sure your transfer prices are saved in the settings.
  4. Monthly fees Fixed monthly amounts, from either supplier or grid operator, do not depend on consumption, i.e. are not per-kWh. Kilowahti spreads them into monthly_fixed_cost_today, separate from the per-kWh sensors.
  5. Electricity tax In some countries this is billed inside the transfer price rather than separately.

Everything you enter into Kilowahti is gross, VAT included. Everything published directly on the electricity market is net, and Kilowahti adds the taxes automatically.

docs.title: An entity is missing entirely
docs.text:
Some groups of entities only exist when enabled in the settings:

Missing Turn on Export, spread, solar sensors Enable generation & export features in Advanced options Battery charge/discharge sensors In addition to the above, set a battery capacity greater than zero Rolling 30/60/120-minute averages Show next 30min, 1h and 2h average prices in Advanced options, when the price resolution is 15 minutes Exchange rate sensor Not available unless a local currency outside the eurozone is in use transfer_price, control_factor_transfer Exist always, but read unknown until transfer prices are configured

New entities appear as soon as the option is saved; no restart needed.

docs.title: Rank stays at 1 all day
docs.text:
Normal on a fixed-price contract. Rank orders today's slots by the energy price you actually pay, and during a fixed-price period every slot costs the same, so they all tie at 1. rank_acceptable then stays on all the time, and the "Rank became acceptable" trigger never fires.

If you still want to pick out the cheaper hours on such a day, use total_price_rank, which includes the transfer price, or the "price is lowest today" condition.

docs.title: The score sensor has no value
docs.text:
Optimization scores need an energy meter to work. First make sure the energy meter entity has state_class: total_increasing and is attached in Kilowahti's settings under Configure → Score profiles → Edit: Total.

The optimization score accumulates through the day and is finalised at midnight, so a freshly attached meter shows nothing until it has measured consumption for a while.

From a power sensor to an energy sensor with a helper

A plain power reading in watts will not work, but if no better energy measurement is available, you can manually add a helper that turns the momentary power into consumption in kilowatt-hours, and Kilowahti can use that.

docs.title: History graphs show a unit mismatch
docs.text:
Changing the display unit or display currency changes the unit of every price entity, and Home Assistant's long-term statistics do not convert what was already recorded. The old data keeps its old unit and the graph complains.

Preferably pick your unit and currency once at setup and keep them unchanged. If you must change them afterwards, expect to clear the statistics of the affected sensors.

docs.title: Editing a tier does not change anything
docs.text: Fixed in Kilowahti version 2026.9.0. On earlier versions, edits to an existing transfer group or tier were not picked up until an unrelated event refreshed the sensors, such as a slot boundary, a fixed-period change, or midnight. Adding and removing groups always worked. Update Kilowahti to the new version.

docs.title: Charts stopped showing price arrays from history
docs.text:
The today_prices and tomorrow_prices attributes are deliberately excluded from the recorder, so they exist only in the current state, not in history. Cards that read the live attribute work normally; anything querying historical attribute values will not find them.

When moving to 15-minute pricing these arrays exceeded Home Assistant's 16 KB limit on recorded attributes, which made the recorder discard the sensor's attributes wholesale and log a warning on every update of the sensor.

docs.title: Still stuck
docs.text: Open an issue or a discussion on GitHub, or, if you would rather not create a GitHub account, use the feedback form. Logs from Settings → System → Logs filtered to kilowahti help enormously in solving the problem.

docs.title: kilowahti-py
docs.text:
2026-03-142026-08-03

kilowahti-py is the pure-Python library that powers the Kilowahti Home Assistant integration. It can be used independently in any Python project that needs to work with European electricity spot prices.

  • PyPI package name: kilowahti
  • Requires: Python ≥ 3.12, aiohttp ≥ 3.9
  • Source: github.com/Kilowahti/kilowahti-py

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pip install kilowahti

docs.title: What's in the library
docs.text:
Module Contents kilowahti.models Data classes: PriceSlot, TransferGroup, FixedPeriod, … kilowahti.calc Pure calculation functions — pricing, ranking, scoring kilowahti.sources PriceSource ABC with KilowahtiCdnSource and SpotHintaSource implementations kilowahti.const API URLs, region list, country presets, unit constants

Models, calculation functions, and constants are re-exported from the top-level kilowahti namespace; the price source classes live under kilowahti.sources:

from kilowahti import PriceSlot, spot_effective, COUNTRY_PRESETS
from kilowahti.sources.kilowahti_cdn import KilowahtiCdnSource

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
import asyncio
import aiohttp
from kilowahti import PriceResolution, spot_effective
from kilowahti.sources.kilowahti_cdn import KilowahtiCdnSource

async def main():
    source = KilowahtiCdnSource()
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        slots = await source.fetch_today(session, region="FI", resolution=PriceResolution.MIN15)

    vat_rate = 0.255  # 25.5 % Finnish VAT
    for slot in slots:
        price = spot_effective(slot, vat_rate=vat_rate, commission=0.0)
        print(f"{slot.dt_utc.strftime('%H:%M')}  rank {slot.rank:2d}  {price:.2f} c/kWh")

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Calculations
docs.text:
2026-03-142026-05-05

All functions in kilowahti.calc are pure (no I/O, no state). They take explicit parameters and return values.

from kilowahti import calc
# or import individually:
from kilowahti.calc import spot_effective, cheapest_window, compute_score

docs.title: spot_effective
docs.text:
def spot_effective(slot: PriceSlot, vat_rate: float, commission: float) -> float

Apply VAT to the raw spot price and add the (gross) commission.

result = slot.price_no_tax × (1 + vat_rate) + commission
Parameter Description slot The price slot vat_rate Decimal fraction, e.g. 0.255 for 25.5 % commission Gross retailer margin in c/kWh (already VAT-inclusive) 
# 3.0 c/kWh spot, 25.5% VAT, 0.35 c/kWh commission → 4.115 c/kWh
price = spot_effective(slot, vat_rate=0.255, commission=0.35)

docs.title: effective_prices
docs.text:
def effective_prices(slots: list[PriceSlot], vat_rate: float, commission: float) -> list[float]

Convenience wrapper — returns spot_effective for every slot in the list.

docs.title: total_price
docs.text:
def total_price(effective: float, transfer: float | None) -> float

Combines the effective energy price and transfer price. If transfer is None, treated as 0.0.

docs.title: slots_in_range
docs.text:
def slots_in_range(all_slots: list[PriceSlot], start: datetime, end: datetime) -> list[PriceSlot]

Filter slots to those whose dt_utc falls in [start, end). Both timezone-aware and naive datetimes are accepted; naive datetimes are assumed UTC.

docs.title: cheapest_window
docs.text:
def cheapest_window(
    slots: list[PriceSlot],
    slots_needed: int,
    price_fn: Callable[[PriceSlot], float],
    *,
    prefer_last: bool = False,
) -> tuple[list[PriceSlot], float] | None

Find the consecutive block of slots_needed slots with the lowest average price as computed by price_fn.

price_fn is called once per slot to determine its price for comparison — pass any callable that maps a PriceSlot to a float. Common choices: lambda s: s.price_no_tax (raw spot), or a custom function that adds VAT and transfer.

When prefer_last=True, the latest window is returned on ties instead of the earliest.

Returns (window_slots, avg_price) or None if slots_needed > len(slots).

# Find the cheapest 2-hour window in the day
result = cheapest_window(today_slots, slots_needed=2, price_fn=lambda s: s.price_no_tax)
if result:
    window, avg = result
    print(f"Cheapest 2h starts at {window[0].dt_utc}, avg {avg:.2f} c/kWh")

docs.title: normalized_total_price_rank
docs.text:
def normalized_total_price_rank(
    current: PriceSlot,
    today_slots: list[PriceSlot],
    price_fn: Callable[[PriceSlot], float],
    slots_per_day: int,
) -> int | None

Rank of current by price among today's slots, normalized to [1, slots_per_day]. Tier-based: K unique prices map evenly across the range, so the cheapest tier is always 1 and the most expensive is always slots_per_day, regardless of how many distinct price levels exist. Useful for control automations when many slots tie (e.g. fixed-period contracts where energy prices are equal but transfer differs).

price_fn is called once per slot to determine its price — pass any callable that maps a PriceSlot to a float. Returns None when today_slots is empty or current is not among them.

docs.title: rank_to_bucket
docs.text:
def rank_to_bucket(rank: int, slots_per_day: int) -> str  # "q1" | "q2" | "q3" | "q4"

Maps a rank to a price quartile bucket. "q1" is the cheapest quartile.

Rank range Bucket 1 – slots_per_day/4 "q1" slots_per_day/4+1 – slots_per_day/2 "q2" slots_per_day/2+1 – 3×slots_per_day/4 "q3" 3×slots_per_day/4+1 – slots_per_day "q4"

docs.title: price_quartile
docs.text:
def price_quartile(rank: int, slots_per_day: int) -> int  # 1..4

Same as rank_to_bucket but returns an integer (1–4).

docs.title: transfer_price_for_slot
docs.text:
def transfer_price_for_slot(
    slot: PriceSlot,
    group: TransferGroup | None,
    as_local_fn: Callable[[datetime], datetime],
) -> float | None

Returns the transfer price (c/kWh) for the slot's time according to group, or None if no group is configured.

docs.title: transfer_rank_info
docs.text:
def transfer_rank_info(
    group: TransferGroup | None,
    now_local: datetime,
) -> tuple[int, int] | None

Returns (rank, tier_count) where rank is the current transfer tier's rank among all unique transfer prices active today, and tier_count is the total number of distinct prices. 1 = cheapest tier. Returns None if no group or no matching tier.

docs.title: normalize_transfer_rank
docs.text:
def normalize_transfer_rank(rank: int, total: int) -> float

Normalises transfer rank to [0.0, 1.0]. 0.0 = cheapest, 1.0 = most expensive. When total == 1, always returns 0.0.

docs.title: control_factor
docs.text:
def control_factor(rank: int, slots_per_day: int, function: str, scaling: float) -> float

Compute a normalized control factor in [0.0, 1.0] based on price rank:

  • 1.0 = cheapest slot (rank 1)
  • 0.0 = most expensive slot (rank = slots_per_day)
Parameter Description rank Current slot's price rank slots_per_day 24 (HOUR) or 96 (MIN15) function "linear" or "sinusoidal" scaling Exponent applied after the curve; 1.0 = no scaling 
from kilowahti.const import CONTROL_FACTOR_SINUSOIDAL
cf = control_factor(rank=1, slots_per_day=24, function=CONTROL_FACTOR_SINUSOIDAL, scaling=1.0)
# → 1.0

docs.title: control_factor_bipolar
docs.text:
def control_factor_bipolar(cf: float) -> float

Converts a [0, 1] control factor to bipolar [-1, +1]:

result = 2 × cf − 1

docs.title: compute_score
docs.text:
def compute_score(bucket_data: dict[str, float], formula: str = "default") -> float

Compute an optimization score (0–100) from quartile energy consumption data.

bucket_data maps bucket names ("q1" … "q4") to kWh consumed in each quartile.

Formula Behaviour "default" Scales raw score so that random consumption ≈ 50 "raw" Direct percentage of consumption in cheap quartiles 
# All consumption in the cheapest quartile
score = compute_score({"q1": 10.0, "q2": 0.0, "q3": 0.0, "q4": 0.0})
# → 100.0

docs.title: fixed_period_for_date

def fixed_period_for_date(periods: list[FixedPeriod], d: date) -> FixedPeriod | None

Returns the first FixedPeriod whose start_date <= d <= end_date, or None.

Abstract base class for all price data sources. Implement this to add a new data backend.

        self,

docs.text:
Method Returns Raises fetch_today Slots sorted by dt_utc ascending aiohttp.ClientResponseError on HTTP error fetch_tomorrow Slots or None if not yet published aiohttp.ClientResponseError on HTTP error (except 404)
